premise: At a normalized unit-free canonical CNF state with n live variables, m clauses and total literal incidence L, let the v0.5 selector choose a minimum-incidence pivot of degree d=p+q. If L=n*d, then every live variable has incidence degree exactly d.

definitions.T: total literal incidence in the c retained clauses
definitions.t_y: number of retained clauses containing nonpivot variable y
definitions.J: number of NEW distinct non-tautological resolvents not already present among the retained clauses
definitions.Wmax_r_K: maximum total width of K distinct signed non-tautological clauses over r variables

statement: Because all variables have degree d, a nonpivot variable y that occurs in t_y retained clauses occurs in exactly d-t_y pivot-parent clauses and is therefore omitted from exactly t_y of the d pivot-parent clauses.
If a_y and b_y are omissions of y from the p positive and q negative parent buckets, then a_y+b_y=t_y and the number of cross-polarity parent pairs omitting y is a_y*b_y <= t_y^2/4 <= c*t_y/4.
Summing over the r nonpivot variables gives total pair-support mass S >= r*p*q - floor(c*T/4).

The retained c clauses and the J new resolvents are c+J distinct raw-set clauses. Therefore representatives of those J new resolvents have total width at most Wmax_r(c+J)-T. Every other cross pair has union-support width at most r, so S <= Wmax_r(c+J)-T + (p*q-J)*r.
Hence for any feasible retained literal mass T, every J for which Wmax_r(c+J)-T+(p*q-J)r < r*p*q-floor(c*T/4) is impossible.
At an ordinary unit-free stage, 2c<=T<=min(c*r,L-2d) when c>0; for c=0, T=0. Taking the maximum feasible J over this exact integer interval yields a sound theorem-side ceiling on new resolvents.
